arguments: A faithful two-dimensional representation of a quadratic field is one dimensional over it. In the split case both idempotent summands have positive dimension and hence dimension one. Thus the regular-module interpretation is exact. A full stable Z_p lattice has a common denominator and is a fractional ideal of the maximal quadratic order; that ideal is principal in the field case by the DVR property and in the split case componentwise. Choosing the generator identifies the embedding lattice models. This gives one orbit under the maximal order unit group, including ramified quadratic extensions.

For an ordered cyclic-index p^e Eichler lattice pair with e>=1 and integral split projectors, both lattices split into their two labelled summands. After scaling the larger lattice, the smaller has exponents a,b>=0 with a+b=e. Cyclicity forces min(a,b)=0. The types (e,0) and (0,e) cannot be interchanged by an intertwiner preserving the labelled embedding. Conversely pairs of the same type are identified by diagonal scaling. These are unit-conjugacy orbits, not orbits under the full Eichler normalizer. Integral projectors make the argument valid at p=2.

In the retained unramified quadratic division presentation, conjugation by a maximal-order unit acts trivially on the commutative residue field; conjugation by Pi gives its nontrivial Frobenius. Skolem-Noether gives transitivity under D^times. Writing a conjugator as Pi^n times a unit, using normalization of O_D by Pi, and Pi^2=pi central, leaves precisely the two parities. Their distinct residue embeddings show they are distinct unit-conjugacy orbits. No division by p or separability claim at residue characteristic two is hidden.
limits: The relevant orbits are labelled quadratic-order embeddings modulo the local order unit group. An enlarged normalizer quotient would change the orbit count.
